title: Support Measures for Phase Two (Heightened Alert) and Phase Three (Heightened Alert), and Support Measures for Phase Two (Heightened Alert)
what_it_is: Support Measures for Phase Two (Heightened Alert) and Phase Three (Heightened Alert), and Support Measures for Phase Two (Heightened Alert)

sections.label: Joint debate on two Motions
sections.summary: The House decided to debate two Motions together, with Members allowed to consider both in a single speech.

sentences.speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
sentences.text: As the House has decided to jointly take this Motion and the next Motion on Support Measures for Phase Two (Heightened Alert), I will put the question on the next Motion to the House.

sentences.speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
sentences.text: In accordance with the decision of this House to have a simultaneous debate on both Motions, I will now call on Members to make their speeches.

sentences.speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
sentences.text: Members are allowed to consider both Motions in a single speech.

sections.label: Support measures for Phase Two
sections.summary: Two doses of support measures enhance the Jobs Support Scheme, extend rental reliefs and provide targeted support for delivery services, taxi drivers, hawkers and market stall holders.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: The two doses of support measures to enhance the Jobs Support Scheme (JSS) – extending rental reliefs and providing targeted support for the local delivery services, taxi drivers, hawkers and market stall holders – go some way to help those impacted by the new restrictions.

sections.label: Extending JSS to F&B supporters
sections.summary: A Member asks the Minister for Finance to consider extending the Jobs Support Scheme to businesses that directly support the F&B sector.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: This time round, some are contemplating to release workers with these restrictions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: I hope that the Minister for Finance can consider extending the JSS to those businesses that directly support the F&B sector as well.

sections.label: 40% JSS for event organisers
sections.summary: A Member asks the Minister for Finance whether the 40% Jobs Support Scheme support includes domestic event organisers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: Can I clarify with the Minister if this 40% JSS support would also include domestic event organisers, such as those that organise events in schools, the Institutes of Higher Learning (IHLs), for the grassroots, for corporate events and so on?

sections.label: Pandemic economic response fund proposal
sections.summary: A Member asks the Minister for Finance to consider a pandemic economic response fund instead of returning to Parliament for Supplementary Bills.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: Here, I would like to ask the Minister for Finance if he could instead consider setting aside funding to establish a pandemic economic response fund or programme so that the Government will have the ready funding to provide timely and direct reliefs to small businesses, self-employed persons or workers impacted by the sudden COVID-19-related tightened measures rather than having to come back to Parliament again for additional Supplementary Bills.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: For this $2 billion of additional support measures, we are counting on pockets of fiscal spaces, such as delays in construction projects, the one-off capitalisation of the two Significant Infrastructure Government Loan Act (SINGA) infrastructure items and the postponement of school activities, to foot the bill.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: Even the $200 million of buffer is now being used up for this latest package.

sections.label: FY 2019 NIRC figure
sections.summary: In FY 2019, the NIRC was $17.04 billion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: In FY 2019, the NIRC was $17.04 billion.

sections.label: Debt Servicing Costs line item
sections.summary: The 5 July 2021 revised estimates include a new line item called Debt Servicing Costs in the summary of the fiscal position.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: In the 5 July 2021 revised estimates, I also note a new line item in the summary of the fiscal position, which is the "Debt Servicing Costs" item.

sections.label: KTV cluster case growth
sections.summary: Less than a week later, the KTV cluster emerged with eight locally transmitted cases and swelled to 248 cases five days later.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Unfortunately, less than a week later, the KTV cluster emerged with eight locally transmitted cases, which swelled rapidly to 248 cases just five days later.

sections.label: MTF return to Phase Two
sections.summary: A few days later, the MTF decided to step back into Phase Two (Heightened Alert) from 22 July to 18 August after spikes in locally transmitted cases.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Yet, just a few days later, the MTF decided to step back into Phase Two (Heightened Alert) from 22 July to 18 August following spikes in locally transmitted cases, including among the elderly.

sections.label: Comparing infection counts and lockdowns
sections.summary: Many wondered why 56 locally transmitted cases on 14 July did not require a lockdown when 24 infections on 14 May triggered a month of heightened alert.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Because of this, many wondered why our new infection count of 56 locally transmitted cases on 14 July did not require a lockdown when previously a much lower count of 24 infections on 14 May triggered a state of heightened alert for one month.

sections.label: Request for risk index
sections.summary: Earlier this month, the speaker asked if MOH could publish a risk index in its daily virus update for a more holistic view of risk.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Earlier this month, I asked if MOH could publish a risk index in its daily virus update that can give the public a more holistic view of the risk we face.

sections.label: Relief fund and no-pay leave
sections.summary: The speaker welcomes the Market and Hawker Centre Relief Fund's $500 per stallholder, asks about extending relief to private food centre stallholders, and asks about no-pay leave for Singaporean workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: First, I am glad the Minister has introduced a new Market and Hawker Centre Relief Fund, which provides a one-off cash assistance of $500 per stallholder.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Can similar relief be extended to stallholders in neighbourhood food centres which are run by private food service management companies like Koufu and Kopitiam?

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Second, I also note that the Minister has extended the COVID-19 Recovery Grant (Temporary) scheme's income-loss coverage period to end-August.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Is the Minister aware of instances where companies place their Singaporean workers on no-pay leave during Heightened Alert periods while continuing to employ foreign workers at full pay?

sections.label: Vaccination rate doubling
sections.summary: The vaccination rate has more than doubled to about half the population, compared with 24% fully vaccinated in mid-May.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: Compared to mid-May, when only 24% of our population was fully vaccinated and Phase Two (Heightened Alert) had to be first imposed, our vaccination rate has since more than doubled to about half of our population this round.

sections.label: JGI scheme extension urged
sections.summary: The speaker urges extending the JGI scheme, which hired 270,000 locals by February 2021, and calibrating its phase-out.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: Under JGI scheme, 270,000 Singaporeans and Permanent Residents were hired by 42,000 businesses as of February 2021 as reported, with generous wage support of up to 50% of the first $6,000 of their gross monthly income for up to 18 months and that is generous.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: One-third of those hired had been out of work for more than six months and about 60% previously employed in a different sector.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: As the JGI scheme has primarily supported SMEs in their manpower needs and the scheme has helped previously unemployed as well as mid-career switches with job opportunities, I urge the Government to extend the scheme and to carefully calibrate how it is phased out, so that the benefits remain deeply rooted.

sections.label: RIE 2025 Plan support
sections.summary: The speaker supports the Government's RIE 2025 Plan, which sets aside $25 billion for innovation and new discoveries.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: Despite the increasingly tight fiscal position, I support the Government’s continued commitment to the Research, Innovation and Enterprise (RIE) 2025 Plan, setting aside $25 billion to support innovation and new discoveries.

sections.label: Registered Home Offices increase
sections.summary: Registered Home Offices increased by 25% in 2020, with the pandemic revealing new entrepreneurial opportunities.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: The number of registered Home Offices saw an increase of 25% in 2020, with the pandemic revealing new entrepreneurial opportunities.

sections.label: Home-based food business regulations
sections.summary: HDB, URA and SFA regulations for home-based food businesses should be reviewed to support artisanal activities with safety and hygiene standards.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: For instance, in the home-based food business, which runs the gamut of home bakeries to private kitchens, the regulations under HDB, URA and SFA should be reviewed to support artisanal home-based activities and a relevant set of regulations to meet with the appropriate levels of commercial standards for safety and hygiene.

sections.label: Support for Supplementary Supply Bill
sections.summary: The speaker states support for the Supplementary Supply Bill.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: With that, I support the Supplementary Supply Bill.

sections.label: Changi Airport breach, Phase Two
sections.summary: Community cases rose after a breach at Changi Airport, so Phase Two (Heightened Alert) began on 16 May, closing dine-in for four weeks.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: After months of progressively opening up in the original Phase Three, Singapore's recovery received a huge setback when community cases jumped after the virus breached our defences at Changi Airport.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: This resulted in an announcement on 14 May that a new phase, christened Phase Two (Heightened Alert), would come into effect two days later, meaning that all food and beverage businesses would once more be required to shut down to dine-in customers, along with restrictions being tightened for a host of other industries and that these would take effect for four weeks.

sections.label: Phase Three dining rule changes
sections.summary: From 14 June dining and gathering limits eased in steps, but on 20 July dine-ins were banned again for four weeks.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: On 10 June, it was decided by the MTF that we would move to Phase Three (Heightened Alert) in two steps from 14 June, with food outlets opening up with two diners allowed to dine in; social gathering and visitor sizes moving to five; and, on 7 July, the number of diners were allowed to increase to five per table, all these to take effect from 12 July.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: By the middle of the week, the cluster had grown to 88 infections and, on 16 July, just four days after dining sizes were increased to five, a slew of dining rules and regulations that one would need an advanced degree to navigate were mandated to be implemented by restaurants on 19 July.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: And, finally, on 20 July, after barely a day of having to comply with the most complicated dining rules ever to have been devised, restaurants were suddenly told they had to throw all of that and much of their inventory out of the window and that dine-ins would no longer be allowed for the next four weeks.

sections.label: Microsoft survey on worker burnout
sections.summary: A Microsoft survey found Singapore workers more burnt out than global peers, with half exhausted and 58% overworked.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: A recent survey by Microsoft found that workers in Singapore were more burnt out and exhausted, compared with their peers globally, with one in two workers saying they felt exhausted and 58% saying that they felt overworked.

sections.label: Construction and cleaning industry struggles
sections.summary: Construction firms and the cleaning industry face high migrant worker quarantine costs and a worker shortage.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: In particular, construction firms and the cleaning industry are facing high costs of having to quarantine migrant workers and are also struggling with a shortage of workers.

sections.label: Roadmap for living with COVID-19
sections.summary: The Finance Minister said a roadmap for Singapore's transition to life with COVID-19 was being prepared, and the Health Minister said it was being implemented.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Yet, I note that the Finance Minister indicated that the Government was, in fact, preparing a roadmap for Singapore's transition to life with COVID-19.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Yesterday, the Health Minister updated this House that a roadmap was currently being implemented.

sections.label: Confusing vaccine and restriction communications
sections.summary: The speaker cites shifting vaccine eligibility advice, outdated safety booklets and lagging business guidelines, urging clear, coherent communication.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Yet, I have heard many accounts of individuals being told that they were ineligible for the vaccine due to medical reasons, such as drug allergies, in one week, only to be encouraged to sign up to get themselves vaccinated the week after, with no official statements being made that they could find about the reversal in policy at the time.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: More personally, I registered to take the vaccine after the rules relating to breastfeeding mothers and anaphylaxis were updated, but found out when I got home after my first shot that the safety booklet given to me contained the outdated advice that breastfeeding mothers should stop breastfeeding for five days and those with a history of anaphylaxis were ineligible for the vaccine!

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Likewise, each time a major announcement is made about tightening up or loosening of restrictions, my inbox gets a series of emails from various business or even school mailing lists urging patience while they wait for guidelines from the relevant authorities about how the rules will affect their operations and also to allow them time to digest the rules and adapt their processes yet again to ensure compliance.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: There is also often a lag of a few days before business and individual support measures are announced, leaving much anxiety in the meantime.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: While all these seem like small things, they do not help in engendering confidence, whether to encourage more people to get themselves vaccinated or to convince people that these are the right steps to keep Singapore safe and our economy going.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: I end by saying that having clear, coherent communications throughout the various stages of the pandemic and honest, open conversations about the reasons and matrices for the different restrictions and support measures is just as important as the substantive steps being taken.

sections.label: Jobs Support Scheme business support
sections.summary: The Jobs Support Scheme, rental relief and access to credit have been critical in helping businesses tide over.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: The Jobs Support Scheme (JSS), rental relief and access to credit have been critical in supporting businesses tide over.

sections.label: Managing SMM and testing costs
sections.summary: The passage asks whether measures exist to reduce SMM costs and make ART, PCR tests and self-test kits more affordable for businesses.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: Can the Minister share if there are any measures to reduce and effectively manage the costs of SMMs required of businesses in the new normal?

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: How can the cost of routine antigen rapid tests (ARTs) or the polymerase chain reaction (PCR) tests and the ART self-test kits be made more affordable for businesses as they will be ongoing costs?

sections.label: CRG-T scheme eligibility criteria
sections.summary: The passage asks whether eligibility for the CRG-T scheme can consider individuals needing support who live in properties above $21,000 annual value but do not own or own only one property.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: Can consideration for eligibility be given to individuals who meet the eligibility criteria for the CRG-T scheme and need the support but live in properties with an annual value above $21,000 but do not own the property or own only one property?

sections.label: F&B venue closures and hardship
sections.summary: The passage states concern that frequent venue closures and dining-in rule changes have caused disproportionate hardship for small F&B operators facing financial pressures.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: F&B is at the heart of Singaporeans’ lives and the number one feedback I have been receiving is that relating to the F&B sector.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: I am concerned that frequent venue closures for faults not of their own doing and changes in rules pertaining to dining-in have led to disproportionate hardship for small operators who may already be facing substantial financial pressures.

sections.label: Microsoft Japan productivity case
sections.summary: The passage states that Microsoft Japan experienced a 40% increase in productivity and an overall 94% employee satisfaction rate.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Most of us would have heard the case of Microsoft Japan, which had experienced a 40% increase in productivity and an overall 94% employee satisfaction rate.

sections.label: SMEs and global tax reforms
sections.summary: The passage states SMEs make up 99% of enterprises, employ over 70% of workers and contributed 43% of GDP in 2020, and mentions questions on corporate income tax and global tax reforms.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The close to 280,000 SMEs represent 99% of enterprises in Singapore and, critically, employ more than 70% of our workers and contributed to 43% of our GDP in 2020 and are critical to the health of our economy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: I have asked a series of questions on Singapore's corporate income tax rates and the impact from global tax reforms endorsed by the G7, G20 and more than 130 countries globally, including Singapore.

sections.label: SME and non-SME tax data
sections.summary: For YA2019, non-SMEs had S$459 billion pre-tax profits and S$11.5 billion tax, while SMEs had S$44 billion profits and S$4.8 billion tax.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: For non-SMEs, their total profits before tax were S$459 billion for YA2019, with the total corporate income tax paid of S$11.5 billion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: For SMEs, however, and this includes companies with a turnover of up to S$100 million, their total profits before tax were S$44 billion for YA2019, with the total corporate income tax paid of S$4.8 billion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: In other words, while SMEs accounted for a mere 9% of total profits before tax in YA2019, they contributed to 29% of corporate income tax paid.

sections.label: SME employment decline 2019 to 2020
sections.summary: SingStat data showed SME employment fell from $2.52 million in 2019 to $2.36 million in 2020, a decline of about 160,000 workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Further, based on data from SingStat, we observed that employment of SMEs declined from $2.52 million in 2019, to $2.36 million in 2020, or a decline of about 160,000 in the number of workers.

sections.label: Netball coach income drop
sections.summary: Mdm Sa'adiah Khamis, lead coach and owner of Singapore Netball Academy with 12 coaches, shared that coaches' income may drop by 80% during the Heightened Alert period.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: One of our Pasir Ris residents, Mdm Sa’adiah Khamis, the lead coach and owner of Singapore Netball Academy, which has 12 netball coaches, has shared that during the Heightened Alert period, the income of coaches may drop by 80%!

sections.label: Pasir Ris stallholder income loss
sections.summary: Pasir Ris market stallholders shared that their income loss during the Heightened Alert period was between 40% and 60%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Our market stallholders at Pasir Ris have shared that their income loss during the Heightened Alert period stands at between 40% and 60%.

sections.label: Tiered CRG-Temporary Support Scheme
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether the CRG-Temporary Support Scheme's 50% income loss criterion is too stringent and suggests tiered support starting at 30%, 40% and so on.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Given these circumstances, under the CRG-Temporary Support Scheme, 50% loss of income may be too stringent a criterion before some support is extended to them.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Can we instead consider a tiered support at different levels of income loss, for example, starting at 30%, 40% and so on?

sections.label: Hawker and market stallholder support
sections.summary: Many stall owners reported income loss of 40% to 60% during the Heightened Alert period, and the speaker welcomes support including rental assistance, the Market and Hawker Centre Relief Fund and the Food Delivery Booster Package.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Many stall owners have indicated that their loss of income in the Heightened Alert period is between 40% and 60%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Therefore, I am glad to hear about the support package for hawker centre and market stallholders, including rental assistance, the Market and Hawker Centre Relief Fund and the Food Delivery Booster Package.

sections.label: Senior vaccination progress
sections.summary: Two-thirds of seniors have been vaccinated and more are being encouraged to get vaccinated.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Currently, we have been successful in getting two-thirds of our seniors vaccinated and continue to encourage more to receive their vaccination.

sections.label: Temporary pandemic jobs
sections.summary: As the economy and employment improve, some jobs arising from the pandemic are temporary roles.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Lastly, as our economy and employment rates improve further, let us keep in mind that some jobs arising from this pandemic are temporary roles.

sections.label: Support measures debate
sections.summary: Debate on ministerial statements about support measures for Phase Two and Phase Three heightened alert.

sentences.speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
sentences.text: SUPPORT MEASURES FOR PHASE TWO (HEIGHTENED ALERT) AND PHASE THREE (HEIGHTENED ALERT), AND SUPPORT MEASURES FOR PHASE TWO (HEIGHTENED ALERT) (Debate on Ministerial Statements made on 5 July 2021 and on 26 July 2021)

sections.label: Mental health infrastructure options
sections.summary: Calls for exploring a tertiary psychiatric hospital and a Professional Conversion Programme for Counsellors.

sentences.speaker: Ms Raeesah Khan (Sengkang)
sentences.text: I hope that, in addition to those policies listed by the Minister, there can be further policy options explored to improve our mental health infrastructure.

sentences.speaker: Ms Raeesah Khan (Sengkang)
sentences.text: I specifically call on the relevant Government agencies to look at the feasibility in two areas: firstly, establishing another tertiary psychiatric hospital; and, secondly, the implementation of a Professional Conversion Programme (PCP) for Counsellors, akin to the PCP for Social Workers and Allied Health Professionals.

sections.label: Pandemic-hit sector slumps
sections.summary: The sector has been heavily affected since the pandemic and faces prolonged slumps and further restrictions.

sentences.speaker: Ms Raeesah Khan (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Since the pandemic started, this sector has been affected heavily and is still facing prolonged slumps.

sentences.speaker: Ms Raeesah Khan (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Just as these sectors were beginning to pick up this year, recent clusters have resulted in further rounds of restrictions.

sections.label: Arts and recreation viability
sections.summary: Prolonged slump and restrictions bring the long-term viability and revival of these sectors into question.

sentences.speaker: Ms Raeesah Khan (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The prolonged slump in the arts and recreation sectors, coupled with restrictions that continue to affect businesses and individuals, brings the long-term viability and revival of these sectors into question.

sections.label: Workers leaving arts industries
sections.summary: The passage states many leave these industries, including recent graduates and young adults who invested their education in these areas.

sentences.speaker: Ms Raeesah Khan (Sengkang)
sentences.text: There are probably many more such stories untold.

sentences.speaker: Ms Raeesah Khan (Sengkang)
sentences.text: It speaks to a nationwide phenomenon where many leave these industries, including recent graduates and young adults who have spent the last few years investing their education in these areas.

sections.label: Government support for sector viability
sections.summary: The passage asks how the Government plans to work with these sectors to ensure their medium- and long-term viability.

sentences.speaker: Ms Raeesah Khan (Sengkang)
sentences.text: How does the Government plan to work with these sectors to ensure their medium- and long-term viability?

sections.label: SingapoRediscovers Voucher scheme inclusion
sections.summary: The passage suggests including more businesses from these sectors in the SingapoRediscovers Voucher scheme to assist them and benefit the public.

sentences.speaker: Ms Raeesah Khan (Sengkang)
sentences.text: For example, as my colleague Mr Leon Perera has suggested, we can include more businesses from these sectors in the SingapoRediscovers Voucher scheme so that they can be assisted while enabling the public to benefit from the services they provide.

sections.label: Arts and recreation SMEs need backing
sections.summary: The passage states those in the arts and recreation sectors need collective backing and are among SMEs accounting for a significant proportion of Singapore's employment.

sentences.speaker: Ms Raeesah Khan (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Among those who need our collective backing right now are those in the arts and recreation sectors who are among the many SMEs that account for a significant proportion of Singapore’s employment.

sections.label: One point one billion package relief
sections.summary: The passage states Minister Lawrence Wong's announcement of the $1.1-billion package brought relief to affected businesses like F&B, gyms, hawkers and market stallholders.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Minister Lawrence Wong's announcement of the $1.1-billion package, the subject of which we are debating, has brought a sigh of relief to the most affected businesses, like food and beverage (F&B), gyms, hawkers and market stallholders.

sections.label: F&B and retail sector struggles
sections.summary: The passage states the F&B sector faced reduced seating capacities and retail members battle COVID-19 woes and e-commerce disruption, with some businesses possibly never recovering.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The Restaurants Association of Singapore said that the F&B sector has been battered with reduced seating capacities of some 50% for over 16 months.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Singapore Retail Association members are in no better shape as they battle COVID-19 woes and disruption by e-commerce.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Those who have invested in digitalisation early stand a better chance, while some 10% to 15% of the businesses may never recover.

sections.label: Business community support pleas
sections.summary: As Singapore moves from pandemic to endemic, the business community says Government support and tripartite collaboration remain key, and voices three pleas for support.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: As Singapore prepares to transition from pandemic to endemic, the business community believes that Government support and tripartite collaboration continue to be key.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: And I would like to voice the following three pleas for support, which need to be addressed in parallel with "Let's Test, Let's Trace, Let's Vaccinate".

sections.label: Testing and Stay-Home Notice
sections.summary: In-country testing and Stay-Home Notice arrangements in source countries before bringing new foreign workers to Singapore on chartered green-lane buses or flights.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In-country testing and Stay-Home Notice arrangements in source countries before bringing new foreign workers to Singapore on chartered green-lane buses from Malaysia or chartered green-lane flights.

sections.label: Fair hiring joint statement
sections.summary: SBF, with 29 TACs, put out a joint statement on fair hiring and employment practices on 19 January 2021, recognising Singaporeans' angst over workplace discrimination.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Recognising the angst of Singaporeans on the issue of workplace discrimination, SBF, with 29 TACs, put out a joint statement on fair hiring and employment practices earlier this year, on 19 January 2021.

sections.label: Hawkers going online with e-payment
sections.summary: FMAS says that over the past 16 months some 60% of hawkers have gone online with e-payment systems, which is a great start.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The Federation of Merchants' Associations of Singapore (FMAS) that looks after merchants as well as hawkers, tell me that, over the past 16 months, some 60% of hawkers have gone online with e-payment systems and that is a great start.

sections.label: REDAS seeks sale extension
sections.summary: REDAS members hope the Government will extend by a further six months the period for sale of units in projects, beyond the existing extension for completion delays.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: For members of the Real Estate Developers Association of Singapore (REDAS), while it is appreciated that the Government has already given an extension for delays in project completion, they hope that the Government will give an extension of a further six months for the sale of units in the projects.

sections.label: Business Traveller Pass expansion
sections.summary: The Business Traveller Pass with restricted travel itinerary has been piloted with good feedback, and it is hoped MTI will expand coverage to more business travellers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Some suggestions include: the Business Traveller Pass (BTP) with restricted travel itinerary has been piloted in the past months and feedback has been good.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: It is hoped that MTI can consider expanding the coverage to more business travellers as this would greatly enhance the reopening of business travel.

sections.label: Vaccination passport and overseas localisation
sections.summary: It is hoped Singapore can negotiate a vaccination passport with trading partners, and that Enterprise Singapore will help companies localise in international markets.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: As our population becomes increasingly vaccinated, it is also hoped that Singapore will be able to negotiate with key trading partners a "vaccination passport" that will enable Singaporeans, Permanent Residents and EP holders to travel with reduced requirements for Stay-Home Notice.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The industry hopes that Enterprise Singapore (ESG) will continue to support and actively assist companies to localise in international markets through initiatives like the Global Connect@SBF.

sections.label: Funding delayed $0.6 billion from SINGA
sections.summary: It asks why the delayed $0.6 billion is not funded directly from more SINGA borrowing.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Specifically, why not fund the delayed $0.6 billion directly from more SINGA borrowing instead?

sections.label: Short-term expenditure boost for construction
sections.summary: It states that doing so would ease supply-side restraints and strengthen demand in the construction sector, which shrank 11% in the second quarter.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Moreover, doing so would not only ease the restraints on the supply side, it will also serve to strengthen the demand side in the hard-hit construction sector, still among our hardest hit, having shrunk 11% in the second quarter, which will, undoubtedly, benefit from a short-term expenditure boost.

sections.label: Projects brought forward for capitalisation
sections.summary: It asks whether the Deep Tunnel Sewerage System and North-South Corridor are the only projects that can be brought forward to be capitalised now.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: More pointedly, are the Deep Tunnel Sewerage System and North-South Corridor the only projects that can be brought forward to be capitalised now?

sections.label: US long-term interest rate rise
sections.summary: It states that from the start of this year to the end of the first quarter, the US long-term interest rate almost doubled from 0.9% to 1.7%.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Between the start of this year till the end of the first quarter, the US long-term interest rate almost doubled, from 0.9% to 1.7%.

sections.label: SINGA loan limit and student loans
sections.summary: It warns of undershooting the approved $90 billion SINGA loan limit and suggests dedicating part of SINGA financing to income-contingent repayment student loans.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: If so, we may inadvertently end up significantly undershooting the approved SINGA loan limit of $90 billion and all the benefits associated thus.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: If I may indulge in this opportunity to elaborate on one more suggestion: could we consider dedicating a part of SINGA financing to fund an initial pool of income-contingent repayment student loans?

sections.label: Limiting scheme to needed courses
sections.summary: The scheme could be limited at the outset to courses with a clear economic need, such as information and computer science.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: To maximise repayment probabilities, we could limit, at the outset, the scheme only to courses with a clear economic need, such as information and computer science, biopharmaceutical sciences and digital and social media marketing, among others.

sections.label: Repayment risk transferred to undergraduates
sections.summary: Repayment risk would be transferred to undergraduates as main beneficiaries, while being underwritten by the Government.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The risk of repayment would be transferred to the main beneficiaries of this human capital investment, the undergraduates themselves, while being underwritten by the Government.

sections.label: Goh Keng Swee on defence taxes
sections.summary: In his 1968 Budget speech, Dr Goh Keng Swee addressed the need to increase taxes to finance defence expenditure.

sentences.speaker: Prof Hoon Hian Teck (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In the Budget Day speech given in Parliament on 3 December 1968, the then Minister for Finance, Dr Goh Keng Swee, addressed two fiscal implications of the accelerated withdrawal of British military forces.

sentences.speaker: Prof Hoon Hian Teck (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Two, the nation would have to address the need to increase taxes to finance a forecasted defence expenditure reaching some 10% of gross national product as the country assumes full responsibility to build up its own defence force.

sections.label: JSS helping businesses retain workers
sections.summary: The Government has fiscal resources through JSS to directly help businesses retain resident workers.

sentences.speaker: Prof Hoon Hian Teck (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Today, we are very fortunate that the Government has the fiscal resources through JSS to directly help businesses to retain resident workers.

sections.label: Ageing population requiring fiscal resources
sections.summary: An ageing population from increased life expectancy and reduced fertility, and higher health spending, will require additional fiscal resources.

sentences.speaker: Prof Hoon Hian Teck (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Today, we will need to confront the reality, even under the challenges of COVID-19, that an ageing population resulting from increased life expectancy as well as reduced fertility rate and, therefore, consequently, the higher spending on health, that this will require additional fiscal resources.

sections.label: Fiscal prudence and drawing reserves
sections.summary: Fiscal prudence over decades built resources to meet emergency needs, drawn down during the Global Financial Crisis and last year.

sentences.speaker: Prof Hoon Hian Teck (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: We also exercised fiscal prudence through the decades so that we were able to save and build resources to meet emergency needs.

sentences.speaker: Prof Hoon Hian Teck (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: We were able to draw down on these reserves when the storm was most severe, notably during the Global Financial Crisis and last year, when it was necessary to implement the circuit breaker, a lockdown of business activity, when the storm was at its most severe strength.

sections.label: Goh Keng Swee Budget quote
sections.summary: The passage quotes the end of Dr Goh Keng Swee's Budget speech, saying a new era will dawn when British military withdrawal completes in 1971.

sentences.speaker: Prof Hoon Hian Teck (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Allow me, Mdm Deputy Speaker, to end with this quote, which ends Dr Goh Keng Swee's Budget speech.

sentences.speaker: Prof Hoon Hian Teck (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I quote: “When the British military withdrawal is completed in 1971, a new era will dawn on us.

sections.label: Political survival after 1971
sections.summary: The quote states that after 1971 Singapore faces a test of political survival, and if resources were well used it will pass as it passes economic survival.

sentences.speaker: Prof Hoon Hian Teck (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: After 1971, we have to go through another test, perhaps a more exacting and rigorous test, and that is our survival potential as a separate political entity in a difficult and turbulent part of the world.

sentences.speaker: Prof Hoon Hian Teck (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: If in the intervening years we have put to good account our resources in money, manpower, skills and organisation, I believe we shall pass the test of political survival as adequately as we now are passing the test of economic survival.” Let us all take heart from how we, as a nation, tackled that earlier challenge!

sections.label: Residents ask about lockdown
sections.summary: Many residents asked whether a lockdown was coming on a day with 163 new locally transmitted COVID-19 cases, and the next day Phase Two (Heightened Alert) was announced from 22 July to 18 August with no in-room dining.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Many residents present asked me whether it was true that there would be a lockdown of sorts in a few days' time.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: This was the day when there were reportedly 163 new locally transmitted COVID-19 cases, then, I believe, a single-day record.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: True enough, the next day, the Government announced that Phase Two (Heightened Alert) would be resumed from 22 July till 18 August with no in-room dining.

sections.label: KTV cluster nightlife suspension
sections.summary: As the KTV cluster unfolded, the Multi-Ministry Taskforce announced a two-week suspension from 16 to 30 July 2021 for nightlife establishments that had pivoted into F&B, affecting over 400.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: As the KTV cluster unfolded, the Multi-Ministry Taskforce announced a two-week suspension of operations from 16 July 2021 through 30 July 2021 for all nightlife establishments that had pivoted into F&B establishments, which affected over 400 such establishments.

sections.label: MTI funding for outlets
sections.summary: MTI reported that only 18 out of 400 outlets received funding for kitchen, installation and conversion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: In fact, MTI reported that only 18 out of 400 outlets received funding for kitchen, installation and conversion.

sections.label: Store tenants packaging and fees
sections.summary: Store tenants complained of higher takeaway packaging costs and no waiver of crockery clearing fees, and the speaker hopes rental reliefs will support stalls in privately run food centres and coffeeshops.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Store tenants have complained that they have to spend more on takeaway packaging and yet crockery clearing fees have not been waived.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: I hope rental reliefs will be available to support stalls in privately run food centres and coffeeshops.

sections.label: F&B, markets, rental support
sections.summary: The passage asks whether Government will reimburse Town Councils for access control manpower at markets and hawker centres, and notes mandated landlord rental support.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Changing dining restrictions and work from home add to their woes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: I hope the COVID-19 Recovery Grant, another support scheme, will go some way to reduce some of the losses but F&B operators, hawkers and staff will certainly look forward to the end of dining-in restrictions once and for all when our vaccination rates rise in the coming weeks.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Due to the increase in cases detected at markets and hawker centres, the COVID-19 Multi-Ministry Taskforce has recently directed that all Town Councils are to implement access control with interim fencing and mandatory SafeEntry check-in at all markets and hawker centres by Monday, 26 July, yesterday.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: As additional personnel are required to assist with the access control work, including personnel to man the access control, I would like to ask whether the Government will be reimbursing Town Councils for additional manpower expenses incurred in implementing access control and SafeEntry check-in at markets and hawker centres.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Companies have been coping with suboptimal business conditions for close to one and a half years now.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: I am heartened that the Government is mandating commercial landlords to match the two-week rental support provided by the Government to tenants during the latest Phase Two (Heightened Alert) measures.

sections.label: Three business support recommendations
sections.summary: The passage puts forward three recommendations: add rental relief criteria, extend Temporary Bridging Loan moratoriums, and improve Jobs Support Scheme disbursement and criteria.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: To ensure that these measures are more timely and targeted in helping businesses cope with challenges brought on by COVID-19, I would like to put forward three recommendations: one, to add an additional criteria for rental relief; two, to consider extending moratoriums for Temporary Bridging Loans; and three, to further improve the disbursement and criteria of the Jobs Support Scheme (JSS).

sections.label: MAS loan suspension extension
sections.summary: MAS announced in June that businesses will enjoy a further suspension of 80% of their principal loan till September 2021.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: MAS made an announcement in June this year that businesses will enjoy a further suspension of 80% of their principal loan till September 2021.

sections.label: Events industry SSIC Tier 3
sections.summary: The passage states that events industry businesses such as audio-visual, staging, event design and logistics are categorised as Tier 3 in the SSIC code structure.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: At this juncture, allow me to highlight some of the concerns from businesses within the events industry, concerns that are consistent with what the hon Member Liang Eng Hwa shared earlier.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Those whose businesses include audio-visual, staging and backdrop, event landscaping, event design, event logistics, booth carpentry, artiste management and so on are currently categorised as Tier 3 in the SSIC code structure.

sections.label: Events industry support review
sections.summary: The passage asks to review the support mechanism for the wider events industry ecosystem to preserve capabilities, citing capacity caps, digital revenue shortfalls and losses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: While there are “pilots” for events to take place, the capacity cap makes them commercially not viable.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Those who have pivoted to digital formats have found that the revenue is unable to support existing costs and borrowings incurred prior to COVID-19.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: With high overheads and borrowing costs, event business owners had to bear continued losses and exhaust their own savings to preserve their business to retain capabilities built over many years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Therefore, I would like to ask that we review the support mechanism for the wider events industry ecosystem to preserve capabilities that are much needed to maintain Singapore as a business hub.

sections.label: Three recommendations to preserve capabilities
sections.summary: The passage repeats three recommendations: add rental relief criteria, extend Temporary Bridging Loan moratoriums and review eligibility, and accelerate JSS disbursement and tweak SSIC-tied criteria.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: We need to preserve critical capabilities so that we can emerge stronger.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Hence, I hope the Government can consider my three recommendations: one, to add an additional criteria for rental relief to support more businesses in need; two, to extend moratoriums for Temporary Bridging Loan and review loan eligibility criteria; and, three, to accelerate the disbursement of JSS and tweak the tiered criteria tied to SSIC so that these measures are more timely and targeted in helping our businesses cope with the COVID-19 pandemic.

sections.label: New start-ups during COVID-19
sections.summary: Singapore saw 63,418 new enterprises in 2020, more than 61,573 in 2019 and the highest since 2016, despite the worst recession.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Yet, interestingly, the COVID-19 pandemic has also seen a burst of new start-up formations in many countries around the world, including Singapore: 63,418 new enterprises were set up in 2020 amidst the worst recession in our country's history versus 61,573 in 2019, the highest such figures since 2016.

sections.label: Jurong Fishery Port cluster fishmongers
sections.summary: Fishmongers in the Jurong Fishery Port cluster were tested but not told to cease operations, then told to stop selling after buying seafood.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: For example, when the Jurong Fishery Port cluster erupted, many fishmongers were tested and not told that they are to cease operations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: So, they went ahead and bought their seafood at the wholesale market and, a few hours later, they were told to stop selling, meaning that the seafood they had bought could not be sold.

sections.label: JSS for non-primary business
sections.summary: A company was told no JSS would be paid because the activity was not its primary business; the speaker argues for pro-rated support.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: However, he was told that because it was not his primary business activity, no JSS would be paid.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I would argue that some degree of JSS support should be paid, pro-rated perhaps, in cases where the company has a line of business that warrants JSS but it is not the primary line of business, provided the company can prove that they are still doing some amount of that secondary business.

sections.label: SME tenants' claim submission costs
sections.summary: SME tenants raised concerns about the cost of hired help to submit claims with supporting documents, and the speaker hopes for an automatic service.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: They have also raised their concerns about how costly it would be for them to get hired help just to assist them to submit their claims with supporting documents.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I hope we could look into providing an automatic service for the SME tenants renting mixed-use properties, especially during this crisis, to reduce their financial burden.

sections.label: UOB SME Outlook 2021 survey
sections.summary: The UOB SME Outlook 2021 survey found small SMEs wanted more assistance to apply for existing grants, a top three Budget 2021 wish.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: According to the UOB SME Outlook 2021 survey, small SMEs wanted more assistance to apply for existing grants in schemes and placed this wish as one of their top three wishes for Budget 2021.

sections.label: PSC scholars transferring bond to SME
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether PSC scholars can be given the option to transfer the latter part of their bond to an SME.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: To widen the potential talent pool for such SME scholarships, can we give the option to PSC scholars to transfer the latter part of their bond to an SME?

sections.label: Low-cost shared service industry priority
sections.summary: Economic agencies should treat developing the low-cost shared service industry as an industry development priority.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Our economic agencies should treat the development of the low-cost shared service industry as an industry development priority.

sections.label: Low-cost M&A advisory for SMEs
sections.summary: The Government is asked to consider providing low-cost services to SMEs that cannot engage M&A advisory firms to match them with acquirers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Would the Government look into providing low-cost services to SMEs that cannot engage M&A advisory firms to help match them to potential acquirers?

sections.label: Enterprise SG overseas hot-desking facilities
sections.summary: Enterprise SG is asked whether it can provide small hot-desking facilities and business centres in its key overseas centres for first-time SMEs going abroad.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Can Enterprise SG provide small hot-desking facilities and business centres in its key overseas centres to support SMEs going abroad for the first time?

sections.label: UOB survey on smaller SME support
sections.summary: The UOB SME Outlook 2021 survey found smaller SMEs with turnover under S$10 million stressed greater need for financial support and easier access to funding and grants.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: For example, according to the UOB SME Outlook 2021 survey, smaller SMEs with a turnover of less than S$10 million stressed a greater need for financial support to ease short-term cash flow issues and that they desired easier access to funding and grants.

sections.label: SME lending, IP protection, Mittelstand
sections.summary: The passage proposes revisiting an EXIM bank for SMEs, notes SME intellectual property concerns, and cites thriving SME sectors in other economies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Having an institution that has the sole mandate to lend to and boost our SMEs, rather than relying on schemes driven by commercial banks who will, understandably, pursue primarily commercial priorities, can help us better address SMEs' financing needs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Hence, I believe the establishment of an EXIM bank for SMEs is an idea worth revisiting.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Next, protecting the intellectual property of SMEs is critical to fostering innovation in the SME sector.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: However, anecdotally, there is still a perception in some quarters of the business community that for very IP-dependent kinds of work, such as creative and consulting work, for example, large Government agencies may take ideas contained in the proposals submitted to them by companies and either adopt those ideas internally or pass those ideas on to cheaper vendors to execute, without the permission or knowledge of the company submitting the proposal that contained those ideas.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: SMEs which feel that this may have been done to them would mostly not be inclined to complain or take legal action, due to the costs involved as well as the fear of antagonising the Government.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Other successful economies around the world have thriving SME sectors, showing that these can co-exist with open economies and large global MNC sectors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Our very own equivalent of the German “Mittelstand”, or middle-sized companies sector, can form one of our pathways to the post-COVID-19 future.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cheng Hsing Yao (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Yesterday, I was very heartened to hear from the MTF an unequivocal commitment for the transition into living with the virus.

sections.label: Government business and job support schemes
sections.summary: The Government has supported businesses and jobs through substantial schemes such as JSS and tax rebates, and intervened into private agreements through legislation such as COTMA.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cheng Hsing Yao (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The Government has been very proactive in supporting businesses and saving jobs through very substantial schemes, such as JSS, tax rebates and so on.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cheng Hsing Yao (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In addition, the Government has, through legislation, such as COTMA, directly intervened into private agreements.

sections.label: Government intervention in private contracts
sections.summary: The speaker says repeated interventions in private contracts will make businesses and investors wonder if that is the Government's modus operandi, and asks the Government to outline its philosophy on intervening in private contracts.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cheng Hsing Yao (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Rare instances of intervention in private contracts are understandable, but repeated interventions will make businesses and investors wonder if that will be the Government’s modus operandi going forward.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cheng Hsing Yao (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: It would be useful if the Government could outline its philosophy on intervening in private contracts.

sections.label: SME Working Capital risk-share increase
sections.summary: The speaker proposes that ESG increase its risk-share for SME Working Capital under the Enterprise Financing Scheme to 80% for both mature and newer companies, up from 50% and 80% respectively, and extend the maximum repayment period from five to eight years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: For those utilising SME Working Capital under the Enterprise Financing Scheme (EFS), ESG shares the loan default risk with the Participating Financial Institutions (PFIs).

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: I propose that ESG increase its risk-share to 80% for both mature and newer companies, up from 50% and 80% respectively, and extend the maximum repayment period from five to eight years.

sections.label: Enhanced EFS-Trade Loan risk-share
sections.summary: The speaker says extending the repayment period will reduce the burden on companies during the transition period, and hopes ESG can increase its risk-share for Enhanced EFS-Trade Loan from 70% to 80% and allow the existing trade loan to be included and eligible under this scheme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Extending the repayment period will reduce the burden on these companies during the transition period.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: I also hope that ESG can increase its risk-share for Enhanced EFS-Trade Loan (EFS-TL) from 70% to 80% and allow the existing trade loan to be included and eligible under this scheme.

sections.label: Transfer of Government payment obligations
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether MOF would allow the transfer of Government payment obligations and receivables from their vendors to third parties without suppliers seeking explicit approval from the Government buyers, the Ministries and Statutory Boards.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Would MOF allow the transfer of such Government payment obligations and receivables from their vendors to third parties without the need for the suppliers to seek explicit approval from the Government “buyers”, in other words, the Ministries and Statutory Boards?

sections.label: Tax exemption for remote workers
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether the Government would consider extending the tax exemption period to the end of this year for residents working in Singapore remotely for overseas firms.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Next, would the Government consider extending the tax exemption period to the end of this year for residents working in Singapore remotely for overseas firms?

sections.label: Ministers explained Phase Two tightening
sections.summary: The speaker states that yesterday, the three Ministers who co-chair the Multi-Ministry Task Force explained the sequence of events that led to the tightening of posture to Phase Two (Heightened Alert).

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: Yesterday, the three Ministers who co-chair the Multi-Ministry Task Force (MTF) explained the sequence of events that led to the tightening of posture to Phase Two (Heightened Alert).

sections.label: Vaccination incentive measures
sections.summary: The speaker strongly favours Government measures to incentivise rapid vaccination, including differentiating arrangements between vaccinated and unvaccinated people.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: For these reasons, I am strongly in favour of Government measures to incentivise rapid vaccination, including differentiating arrangements between the vaccinated and the unvaccinated.

sections.label: NTUC training committee network
sections.summary: NTUC will scale its Company Training Committee network and Ops-Tech roadmapping to help companies quicken their pace of adjustment and transformation.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: NTUC will scale our Company Training Committee (CTC) network and Ops-Tech roadmapping to help companies quicken their pace of adjustment and transformation.

sections.label: Protecting workers and workplace discrimination
sections.summary: The speaker says protection should shift from jobs to workers' employability, welcomes MOM's tripartite committee on workplace discrimination, and commits NTUC to participate.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: For example, given rapid changes in skills requirements, it will be almost impossible to protect specific jobs from change.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: We should rightly, therefore, move from trying to protect jobs to protecting workers through improving their employability.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: On this, I am glad that MOM has decided to set up a tripartite committee to consider how best to enhance effective protection against discrimination of various kinds in the workplace, in order to unlock performance and potential.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: Done right, this will improve not only the optics of Fairness at Work but will actually hone it into a competitive advantage for Singapore businesses and workers.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: NTUC is committed to participate actively in this committee and to work towards win-win outcomes.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: They buy us precious time to retool for a shot at better lives and livelihoods ahead.

sections.label: Helping lower-wage and migrant workers
sections.summary: The speaker urges creating a community where no one is left behind, citing 39% real wage growth for lower-wage workers at the 20th percentile from 2009 to 2019.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: With these in mind, it is even more important than before to work towards creating a community where no one is left behind and we lend a helping hand to those who are particularly disadvantaged now, such as our lower-wage brothers and sisters in the workforce as well as our migrant workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: We have seen that in the past decade or so, from 2009 to 2019, the real wages of our resident lower-wage workers who are at the 20th percentile have grown by 39%, compared to the median of 33%.

sections.label: Tripartite Workgroup recommendations hopes
sections.summary: The speaker reiterates the Labour Movement's hope that the Tripartite Workgroup's coming recommendations will expand PWMs to cover more workers at the 20th percentile and below.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: The Tripartite Workgroup is set to release its recommendations in the coming months and I would like to reiterate the hopes of the Labour Movement that these recommendations will lead to tangible outcomes for our workers, such as the expansion of the PWMs to cover more workers at the 20th percentile and below.

sections.label: Workfare Income Supplement expansion call
sections.summary: The speaker says WIS uplifts lower-wage workers, notes 2017 and 2020 improvements, and calls to lower age eligibility to 30 and raise payouts for essential service workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: In addition to ensuring sustainable wage increases, policies like the Workfare Income Supplement (WIS) scheme continue to be an important tool in uplifting our lower-wage workers and significant improvements to the scheme have been made during the reviews in 2017 and 2020.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: I am assured that the Government will continue to review WIS at regular junctures and would like to reiterate my call to expand coverage of WIS by lowering the age eligibility of the scheme to 30 as well as increase the WIS payout for essential service workers.

sections.label: Support for migrant workers
sections.summary: The passage welcomes expanded dormitory coverage, long-term primary healthcare access and electronic salary payment for migrant workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: In addition to the support given to our lower-wage brothers and sisters, I am also encouraged to hear stories of many Singaporeans who have gone out of their way to appreciate our migrant workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: I am heartened by the response from the Second Minister for Manpower Dr Tan See Leng to the Labour Movement's calls to expand the Foreign Employee Dormitories Act (FEDA) to cover all dormitories in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: We believe that this move will help enhance the existing requirements with the additional needs in important areas, such as health and safety and the provision of social services, which should be afforded to all our migrant workers, regardless of their dormitories.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: I also applaud the move to provide long-term access to primary healthcare for our migrant workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: The outbreak in the foreign worker dormitories has highlighted how early and efficient access to medical care is imperative not just for the workers or employers but also for public health.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: This effort, coupled with the ongoing discussion to extend the electronic payment of salaries to more workers, can help better protect the migrant workers who have come to Singapore to earn an honest living.

sections.label: Lower-wage worker support hopes
sections.summary: The Labour Movement hopes Tripartite Workgroup recommendations expand PWMs and urges lowering WIS age eligibility to 30 and raising payouts for essential service workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: In addition, I would also like to take the opportunity to reiterate the hopes of the Labour Movement that the upcoming recommendations by the Tripartite Workgroup on Lower-Wage Workers will lead to tangible outcomes for our workers, such as the expansion of the PWMs to cover more workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: In addition, I also urge the Government to consider expanding the WIS scheme by lowering the age eligibility of the scheme to 30 years, as well as increasing the WIS payout for essential service workers so that more can benefit from this scheme.

sections.label: Vigilance and budget support schemes
sections.summary: The passage urges Singaporeans to report establishments flouting safe management measures and notes seven rounds of budgeted support schemes since the pandemic.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I hope Singaporeans can stay vigilant and report such establishments that flout the safe management measures.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: We have had a total of seven rounds of budgeted support schemes to help businesses and workers in affected sectors since the pandemic last year.

sections.label: Labour Movement CTCs achieved
sections.summary: The Labour Movement has achieved more than 600 CTCs across industries, tying in with the Government's Job Transformation Maps.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: For the record, the Labour Movement has achieved more than 600 CTCs across the different industries and these efforts would tie in nicely with the Government's efforts in the Job Transformation Maps.

sections.label: Fair hiring penalties and committee
sections.summary: The passage seeks further penalties beyond work pass privilege suspension for repeated unfair hiring and notes a Tripartite Committee on Workplace Fairness was announced.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: While the Fair Consideration Framework is a means for locals to be given fair consideration based on merit, more should be done to respond to such hiring practices that favour foreign talents over our local workforce.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I hope that the Government can consider further penalties beyond just suspension of work pass privileges for companies that have been found to have repeatedly chosen not to adhere to fair hiring practices.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Yesterday, the Minister announced the formation of a Tripartite Committee on Workplace Fairness.

sections.label: Seven Budgets with support schemes
sections.summary: The Government announced seven Budgets with support schemes to help businesses and workers overcome the crisis.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In total, the Government announced seven Budgets with support schemes to help businesses and workers overcome this crisis.

sections.label: Labour Movement Company Training Committees
sections.summary: The Labour Movement had already established Company Training Committees before this.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In fact, before this, the Labour Movement has already established Company Training Committees.

sections.label: Tripartite Committee on Workplace Fairness
sections.summary: A Tripartite Committee on Workplace Fairness was announced by MOM, which the speaker says is a step in the right direction.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: We have to also avoid any disparity in employment contracts between locals and foreigners.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This aligns very well with the announcement by MOM yesterday on the formation of a Tripartite Committee on Workplace Fairness.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This is a step in the right direction and demonstrates the Government’s effort to ensure a fair and transparent employment process.

sections.label: Workplace fatalities first half 2021
sections.summary: The first half of 2021 saw 22 workplace fatalities, with 11 deaths in February alone.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: The first half of 2021 saw 22 workplace fatalities, with 11 deaths recorded in the month of February alone.

sections.label: Migrant workers leaving Singapore monthly
sections.summary: According to MND, about 1,900 migrant workers decide to leave Singapore each month since the circuit breaker.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: According to MND, about 1,900 migrant workers decide to leave Singapore each month since the circuit breaker was imposed last year.

sections.label: Employment Hero survey on employee stress
sections.summary: A March 2021 Employment Hero survey found seven in 10 local employees felt stressed by COVID-19 in the past six months.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: According to a March 2021 survey commissioned by human resource software firm, Employment Hero, seven in 10 local employees felt stressed by COVID-19 in the past six months.

sections.label: SG Mental Health Matters poll on costs
sections.summary: A poll by SG Mental Health Matters found almost 80% of participants felt costs would be a barrier to quality mental healthcare.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: A poll by SG Mental Health Matters found that almost 80% of the participants felt that costs would be a barrier to seeking quality mental healthcare.

sections.label: NTUC Employee Assistance Programme package
sections.summary: NTUC is working with the Singapore Psychological Society and the Association of Psychotherapists and Counsellors to create a cheaper EAP package for unionised companies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: NTUC is working closely with the Singapore Psychological Society and the Association of Psychotherapists and Counsellors to put together an Employee Assistance Programme (EAP) package for our unionised companies that is significantly cheaper than similar high quality EAP services found commercially.

sections.label: Community Mediation Centre dispute statistics
sections.summary: A question asks whether the Community Mediation Centre can provide statistics on common mediation issues to support a public education campaign.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: Could the Community Mediation Centre provide statistics on the common issues that go to mediation, so that we can embark on a public education campaign to minimise such disputes?

sections.label: Invisible competition and work-from-anywhere
sections.summary: The passage asks if Singaporeans should worry about invisible competition, and calls for caring for those at risk and preparing the workforce for work-from-anywhere.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: Should Singaporeans be worried about such “invisible” competition that cannot be controlled by our existing work pass systems?

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: But as we prepare for an endemic COVID-19, we must look beyond those directly impacted by the virus and care for those whose physical safety and mental health are at risk as they struggle to cope with the new normal.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: We also need to urgently consider the ever-looming threats and opportunities that the work-from-anywhere trend will bring and help prepare our Singaporean workforce for this new reality.

sections.label: Phase Two Alert and sports sector support
sections.summary: The passage states that returning to Phase Two (Heightened Alert) will require additional financial support for sports and fitness businesses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Chay (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: And we understand that the resurgence of infections and the Delta variant are real risks to public health.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Chay (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: But going back to Phase Two (Heightened Alert) will require additional financial support for many businesses in the sports and fitness sector.

sections.label: Togetherness and establishment membership numbers
sections.summary: The passage reaffirms the belief that we are stronger together and notes nearly 600 establishments serving 500,000 to 600,000 members.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Chay (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Right now, this moment, is an excellent opportunity to reaffirm my belief that we are in this together, Mdm Deputy Speaker; we are stronger together.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Chay (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: There are nearly 600 such establishments in the country.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Chay (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: They serve 500,000 to 600,000 members, our residents.

sections.label: Income decline during this period
sections.summary: The passage states that incomes have declined between 20% and 80% during this period.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Chay (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Incomes have declined between 20% and 80% during this period.

sections.label: National sports associations COVID-19 roadmap
