sections.summary: Most national sports associations could not run events last year, and a suggestion is for the MTF to work with them on a COVID-19 roadmap.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Chay (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Unfortunately, most national sports associations have not been able to run events in the past year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Chay (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: As national sports associations are an integral part of athlete development, a suggestion would be for the MTF to closely work with this sector in order to develop the roadmap for COVID-19.

sections.label: Financial support for sports industry
sections.summary: A request is made to consider providing quick financial support for the sports and fitness industry.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Chay (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Please consider providing quick financial support for the sports and fitness industry.

sections.label: Childcare leave for young children
sections.summary: Parents with children under seven years old have only six days of childcare leave a year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Parents with children under seven years old only have six days of childcare leave a year.

sections.label: Childcare leave for older children
sections.summary: Parents whose youngest child is seven to 12 have two days of childcare leave, and 50% of public servants take childcare sick leave.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Worse still for parents whose youngest child is between seven and 12 years old.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: They only have two days of childcare leave.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: This is why it offers childcare sick leave to public servants and this is why 50% of public servants take up the option of childcare sick leave even though they might have access to annual leave, childcare leave and WFH already.

sections.label: Elderly suicides highest in 30 years
sections.summary: The highest spike was among the elderly, with 154 elderly suicides, the highest in 30 years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The highest spike was seen among the elderly, with 154 elderly suicides, the highest in 30 years.

sections.label: Migrant workers dorm movement restrictions
sections.summary: The passage asks the Government's plan to let migrant workers out of dorms, including regional recreational centres and a timeline to lift restrictions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: What is the Government's plan to let our migrant workers out of their dorms?

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: In the short term, can we, at least, establish regional recreational centres, open up spaces, such as old schools and open fields, to let small batches of migrant workers hang out?

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: In the long term, can we have a concrete timeline and plans to lift movement restrictions on our migrant workers?

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: In particular, what is the plan for fully vaccinated workers when we reopen in Phase Three?

sections.label: Hawker rents and restrictions
sections.summary: Calls circulated to help hawkers hit by re-imposed restrictions while news spread that NEA increased hawker stall rents.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: While calls to help hawkers hit badly by the re-imposed restrictions were circulating, news about NEA increasing hawker stall rents made its rounds.

sections.label: SME survey and support uptake
sections.summary: A February survey found 81% of over 400 SMEs surveyed did not expect growth, and only 61% took up pandemic support packages.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Despite this multitude of assistance and with our economy faring better than last year, an annual survey report published in February revealed that 81% of more than 400 SMEs surveyed in the fourth quarter last year do not expect their businesses to grow this year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Although 95% of SMEs are aware of the pandemic support packages, only 61% took them up.

sections.label: GST hike timing suggestion
sections.summary: With government expenditure rising, the passage suggests the Government consider pushing back the GST hike for a few years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: But as the Government's expenditure goes up, with new support measures announced and extended, I am sure the GST hike has been looming in everyone's minds.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: However, given the current circumstances, perhaps the Government should consider pushing back the GST hike for a few years.

sections.label: Streamlining support and budget support
sections.summary: The Government should streamline support measures for individuals and small businesses, and the speaker supports the Supplementary Budget.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The Government should also streamline support measures for individuals and small businesses, especially to make it simple for them to utilise.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: In doing so, I am confident that the people and the Government can weather all storms together.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: I stand in support of the Supplementary Budget.

sections.label: Dutch court Shell emissions ruling
sections.summary: In May, a Dutch court ordered Shell to reduce greenhouse gas emissions 45% by 2030 from 2019 levels.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: In May, the Dutch court made a landmark ruling, ordering Shell to reduce its greenhouse gas emissions 45% by 2030 from 2019 levels.

sections.label: Net zero investment and SINGA bonds
sections.summary: Reaching net zero globally needs an estimated $100-150 trillion over 30 years, and SINGA bonds give another tool.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: An estimated $100-150 trillion investment over the next 30 years, more than in digital transformation, is needed to reach net zero globally.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Our strong financial position has always given us an edge.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Now, the SINGA bonds give us another powerful tool.

sections.label: Green champions and sustainability recovery
sections.summary: Green champions had 30% shareholder returns while oil and gas majors had negative 18%, and companies are called to support climate action and green growth.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The first generation of "green champions", companies like Next Era, Orsted, generated annual total shareholder returns of 30%, on par with big techs, while oil and gas majors had a return of negative 18%.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Otherwise, the time may come when difficult and painful choices will need to be made on the sectors and industries that we can no longer afford in order to meet our sustainability commitments.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: So, I call on companies to first ensure that their activities do not undermine climate action, then to advocate for stronger policies and promote green growth and jobs, to re-assure the Government that we are on the right track.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: If we work together to put sustainability at the heart of our recovery, our COVID-19 response will be remembered as one that not only overcame a short-term recession and avoided a mid-term recession, but also created meaningful, long-term impact that will benefit us all, in Singapore and the world.

sections.label: PCR swabs under RRT
sections.summary: More than 13.6 million PCR swabs have been performed under the RRT, picking up a small handful of positive cases.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: To date, there have been more than 13.6 million PCR swabs performed as part of the RRT, and a large part was for RRT, which has picked up a small handful of positive cases.

sections.label: Adverse effects from nasal swabs
sections.summary: MOH reported few adverse effects from deep nasal swabs, and the Ministry is encouraged to survey and support affected people.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: MOH has replied that there are few reported adverse effects, but there are adverse effects nonetheless.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I encourage the Ministry to do a survey and to provide support for people who have suffered adverse effects from the deep nasal swabs.

sections.label: Police reports on physical assaults
sections.summary: Police reports on physical assaults were highest in 2020, and acts of racism, violence and self-harm are rising.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In the past three years, the number of Police reports on physical assaults was the highest in 2020, despite us being supposedly prevented from coming into contact with each other.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Acts of racism, violence and self-harm are on the rise.

sections.label: Simple rules and nurturing approach
sections.summary: Reactive shutdowns cause suffering without lessons learnt, so simple rules with reasons and a nurturing approach are urged.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Reactive shutting down of all services causes suffering to many while the important lessons are not learnt.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Prescribing group numbers without sharing the principles of these decisions will not help people make better decisions about their health.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Give us some simple rules, with simple reasons why and let the people make that choice and trust that we can make the right choice.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: We must make sure that the mind, the heart and the body are all healthy together.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: That cannot be achieved with fear incited to make sure we are safe, but with a more nurturing approach to ensure that everyone unites to stay safe together.

sections.label: KTV and Jurong Fishery Port clusters
sections.summary: The KTV cluster has 245 cases and the Jurong Fishery Port cluster 902, while hospitalisations rose from five in July to 18.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Up to now, the KTV cluster has had 245 cases, including two cases today.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: The Jurong Fishery Port cluster has had 902 cases, including 36 today.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Let us look at the cases of hospitalisation and those who are very ill, because, as we have said, that is also an important indicator.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: And that has gone up by three and a half times in the past week alone, from five in July – yes, it is a low base – to 18 yesterday.

sections.label: Reviewing Heightened Alert easing for vaccinated
sections.summary: If cases, clusters, hospitalisation and ICU rates stay acceptable and stable, easing for vaccinated persons will be considered at the mid-term of the Heightened Alert.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Fortunately, as of now, while case numbers are still high, it does not look like the numbers are rising exponentially.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: So, if the overall situation, as I said yesterday, cases, clusters under control; hospitalisation rates, ICU rates, remain acceptable and stable, at the mid-term of our Heightened Alert, which is coming soon, we will review and we will consider some easing for vaccinated persons only.

sections.label: Support measures costing over $2 billion
sections.summary: Support measures will cost more than $2 billion throughout the Heightened Alert period since May, with funds reallocated from the existing Budget.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Our support measures, as all of you know, will cost more than $2 billion throughout this Heightened Alert period since May.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Essentially, we have tried to reallocate as much as we can from the existing Budget to avail funds for the support measures.

sections.label: JSS and Rental Support payouts
sections.summary: Eligible firms have received quarterly JSS payouts since April last year, with the most recent in June, and Rental Support Scheme cash payouts due in August.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: To illustrate, eligible firms have been receiving quarterly Jobs Support Scheme (JSS) payouts since April last year, with the most recent paid in June.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: And the cash payout under the Rental Support Scheme will be paid out soon in August, before the next JSS payout in September.

sections.label: Extended JSS support for companies
sections.summary: JSS support was extended to close to 6,000 companies through appeals, including suppliers, vendors, and F&B, retail and events companies.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: In fact, we have extended JSS Support for close to 6,000 companies through such appeals and companies that many Members talked about, those who are suppliers, vendors, to F&B, retail, events companies doing local events.

sections.label: MinLaw considering framework eligibility criteria
sections.summary: MinLaw is carefully considering the eligibility criteria and details of the framework, which will be announced in due course.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: MinLaw is carefully considering the eligibility criteria and the details of the framework, which they will announce in due course.

sections.label: Deferring projects to next year
sections.summary: Projects must be done gradually and in a controlled manner, with pilots working first, so they cannot be done this year and are deferred to next year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: If we were to do this safely, it has to be done gradually, in a controlled manner, making sure that the pilots work first before we can scale up progressively.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: That is why our assessment is that these projects cannot be done this year and have to be deferred to next year.

sections.label: Tightening spending for contingency needs
sections.summary: Additional support later this fiscal year would likely require tightening Government operating and development spending to free up resources for contingency needs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: If we have to provide additional support later in this fiscal year, we will likely need to tighten Government spending across both operating and development expenditures to free up resources for such contingency needs.

sections.label: Fund balance and Reserves use
sections.summary: Setting up such a fund requires balancing Parliament's oversight of relief measures, and in serious emergencies the Government will draw on Reserves with the President's support.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: If we do set up such a fund, we will have to strike the right balance to ensure that Parliament continues to have oversight over the relief measures.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: If we were in such a serious and emergency condition, as I have said before, we will not hesitate to draw on the full fiscal firepower of our Reserves and we will seek the President's support to do so.

sections.label: Global minimum effective tax rate
sections.summary: Fiscal stresses have led to an emerging international consensus on a global minimum effective tax rate, which was discussed.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: At the same time, fiscal stresses have led to the emerging international consensus on a global minimum effective tax rate, which we discussed.

sections.label: Refreshing Industry Transformation Maps
sections.summary: Existing companies must rethink business models and push the technology frontier, so all 23 Industry Transformation Maps are being refreshed to spur restructuring and new growth areas.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Likewise, existing companies must be prepared to rethink their business models, strive for new horizons and push the technology frontier.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: That is why we are systematically refreshing all 23 of our Industry Transformation Maps (ITMs) to spur restructuring and transformation and to develop new growth areas.

sections.label: SGUnited Jobs and Skills Package
sections.summary: Through the SGUnited Jobs and Skills Package, many opportunities have been provided for jobseekers over the past year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Through the SGUnited Jobs and Skills Package, we have provided many opportunities for jobseekers over the past year.

sections.label: Jobs Growth Incentive review
sections.summary: The Jobs Growth Incentive has supported employers to expand local hiring, runs until September this year, and its extension is being reviewed.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: One tangible help that the Government provides for this is the Jobs Growth Incentive, which has supported employers to expand their local hiring.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: The scheme runs until September this year and we are reviewing its extension.

sections.label: Tripartite Workgroup on Lower-Wage Workers
sections.summary: The Tripartite Workgroup on Lower-Wage Workers, chaired by Zaqy Mohamad, is examining how to uplift more workers, including expanding Progressive Wage Model coverage and progressive wages in uncovered occupations.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: The Tripartite Workgroup on Lower-Wage Workers, chaired by Senior Minister of State Zaqy Mohamad, is looking at how we can move faster to uplift even more workers in a sustainable and meaningful manner.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: This includes increasing the number of workers covered by the Progressive Wage Model (PWM) and offering progressive wages in occupations not covered by the mandatory PWMs.

sections.label: New inter-agency mental wellness task force
sections.summary: MOH and MSF have set up a new inter-agency task force, which transited from the COVID-19 Mental Wellness Taskforce.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: MOH and MSF have set up a new inter-agency task force, which transited from the COVID-19 Mental Wellness Taskforce.

sections.label: Halving emissions by 2050
sections.summary: By 2050, Singapore aims to halve greenhouse gas emissions from its 2030 peak, with a view to net zero as soon as viable, and is reviewing the post-2023 carbon tax level.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Beyond 2030, by 2050, we aim to halve greenhouse gas emissions from our 2030 peak, with a view to achieving net zero emissions as soon as viable.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: For a start, we are reviewing the carbon tax level post-2023, in consultation with the industry, to incentivise the shift to green alternatives.

sections.label: Floating solar farm and green finance
sections.summary: Sunseap is building the world's largest floating solar farm and energy storage system in Batam, and Singapore plans to be Asia's leading green finance centre.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: For example, Sunseap, a solar company, is now building the world's largest floating solar farm and energy storage system in Batam.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: We are also putting in place plans to make Singapore the leading centre for green finance in Asia.

sections.label: GST increase funding healthcare spending
sections.summary: The GST rate increase is largely to fund higher spending in healthcare, especially as the population ages.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: The GST rate increase is largely to fund higher spending in healthcare, especially as our population ages.

sections.label: GST increase insufficient for healthcare
sections.summary: Even with a two-percentage point GST increase, Singapore will not be able to cover all its projected healthcare spending needs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: In fact, even with a two-percentage point GST increase, we will not be able to cover all our projected healthcare spending needs.

sections.label: GST Assurance Package
sections.summary: A temporary $6 billion Assurance Package is set aside to cushion the GST increase for all Singaporean households, with lower-income households receiving more.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: As part of the upcoming increase in the GST rate, we have set aside $6 billion for a temporary Assurance Package to cushion the impact for all Singaporean households, with lower-income households to receive more.

sections.label: Lower-income household benefits
sections.summary: Lower-income households receive close to $4 of benefits for every $1 of tax they contribute.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: As I have shared before, lower-income households receive close to $4 of benefits for every $1 of tax they contribute.

sections.label: Studying Town Councils' finances
sections.summary: The speaker thanks Mr Dennis Tan and says the financial position of the Town Councils will have to be studied.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: I did not have the opportunity to address all the points that were raised by Members, so, I thank Mr Dennis Tan for reminding me on this point.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: We will have to study the financial position of the Town Councils.

sections.label: Assessing Town Councils' financial position
sections.summary: The Government will work with MND to assess Town Councils' overall financial situation before considering whether additional support is needed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: At the same time, we have to look at and assess the overall financial position of Town Councils because already, today, the Government provides considerable grants and support to Town Councils in general.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: So, we will work with MND that oversees the Town Councils, to assess the overall financial situation before we consider whether or not additional support might be needed.

sections.label: SME and non-SME tax rates
sections.summary: A more detailed analysis of relative tax burden shares between SMEs and non-SMEs can be done, but SME effective tax rates are much lower.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: And then, we can do a more detailed analysis to see what the relative shares of tax burden are between SMEs and non-SMEs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: But we come back to the main point: effective tax rates for SMEs are much lower than the effective tax rates for non-SMEs in Singapore.

sections.label: More allowance and community time
sections.summary: More allowance is being given in the near term for recreational centres, and they are looking at allowing time out in the community.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Number one, giving more allowance in the initial, very near term, something that we are doing, but will do more for them to go to the recreational centres, spend more time there.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: But, indeed, we are looking at allowing them to have the time to be out in the community as well.
